[00:00] Liam: alright everyone thanks for joining i can see the usual suspects, uh hows everyone doing today
[00:08] Rajiv: good thanks, busy, but yeah we have some new failing cases to show you today so hoping we can get some guidance
[00:15] Sofia: great, and i'll kick off with the benchmark notes from last run, i uploaded a trimmed csv to the drive earlier
[00:23] Evelyn: yep got it, skimmed it, lots of numbers, uh can you do a quick call out of the p95 and p99 spikes?
[00:31] Sofia: sure so the baseline with KV cache warm is about 42ms median, p95 sits at 210ms, p99 at 480, the weird bit is during burst opens we see a second spike where it goes to 1.3s for a small fraction
[00:46] Samir: that's the tail we're worried about, our UI has a 1s timeout so that 1.3 is biting us
[00:52] Liam: okay makes sense, two quick notes — one it's likely the batching/eviction interplay, two we may be seeing quantized kernel fallbacks under longer sequences, i'll have sofia follow up with kernel-level traces
[01:06] Rajiv: can you expand on the eviction interplay? we tuned our cache TTL to 3 minutes to save memory, could that cause more cold starts?
[01:15] Sofia: yes TTLs that short mean more KV reloads, every reload can add like 60-200ms depending on payload size and whether the prefix is batched, also if the model variant switches (like 8-bit to 4-bit fallbacks) you'll incur extra copy time
[01:31] Evelyn: and is that something we control from the SDK or it's infra side?
[01:36] Sofia: knob in both places — SDK can warm the cache proactively (we have an example but it's not in your current sample), infra side (Redwood runtime) manages lifetime and kernel selection, but we can expose warmup hints through the launch config
[01:49] Rajiv: if we add warmup in our SDK path, does that increase cost a lot? we are cost sensitive
[01:55] Liam: warmups are a small delta compared to repeated cold misses — in many of our customers it's net neutral because you reduce repeated reloads; we can run a quick ROI calc and return numbers
[02:06] Samir: switching gears, we have structured-output failures when the model returns an array when our schema expected an object, this then breaks the function call wrapper and the downstream service throws 500s
[02:19] Sofia: yeah that's classic schema drift, did you run the safety sanitizers in the SDK? the new SDK accepts a schema and will do gate checks and soft-fail with metadata rather than throw by default
[02:32] Rajiv: i don't think the team enabled that, our sample only shows a basic call, not the validation layer
[02:37] Liam: ok that's an easy win, sofia can add a snippet to show schema-first validation + fallback lambda where it returns a structured error object when shape mismatch occurs
[02:48] [00:03] (note: timestamps are approximate, auto-timestamping every ~30s)
[03:00] Evelyn: one other thing — function-calling timeouts, sometimes the call completes but the orchestrator already timed out and we've lost the result, are there recommended patterns?
[03:12] Sofia: recommended is to use idempotent invoke with async callback pattern: model returns an operation id and we poll or subscribe via webhook; the SDK has helpers for exponential backoff and dedup tokens
[03:25] Rajiv: can you put that in the examples please, the dedup token is key for us because we sometimes get duplicate callbacks and our job system double processes
[03:34] Liam: noted, adding dedup + exactly-once patterns to the sample is on the list
[03:39] Samir: about the failing payloads, i'll share the trace with a couple of raw requests where the function wrapper returned null and we had to retry thrice before success
[03:47] Rajiv: those are the ones i mentioned earlier, they have lots of long context and a few embedded attachments base64 that might push us into longer sequences
[03:58] Sofia: attachments can force kernel/path changes, if the token count crosses thresholds some runtime paths change which cause slower kernels — try stripping attachments and see if behavior changes
[04:12] Evelyn: question on Dedicated vs Hosted — we are leaning to Dedicated for latency predictability, but worried about management overhead and cost commitments
[04:22] Liam: fair, Dedicated gives SLO-backed latency and isolated pools; for pilots we often recommend a small Dedicated pool with burst to Hosted as fallback so you keep predictable performance without large commit 
[04:36] Rajiv: does fallback to hosted compromise data residency? we have PHI-ish data so residency and encryption matter
[04:42] Sofia: fallback can be restricted by policy; for PHI workloads we'd recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with on-prem network peering, and also KMS integration — we have SOC2 and HSM options in the enterprise package
[04:58] Samir: ok good to know — our main ask is audit logs for every model invoke, we need full traceability
[05:05] Liam: Redwood console can emit per-token traces and per-request logs, we can configure retention and push to your SIEM via secure forwarding
[05:14] Rajiv: we saw a few entries in the logs with mismatch in model version reported vs what we pinned in the SDK, is it possible the runtime rolled a variant during a canary?
[05:23] Sofia: rollouts can be set to pinned by customer, but in shared infra there can be automatic fallback to compat variants when the pinned fails. if you pin the model version in the deployment it will stop auto-variants, we'll include a note in the docs
[05:33] Evelyn: one of our concerns — graceful degradation: what happens if the Dedicated pool saturates? do requests queue or fail fast?
[05:42] Liam: depends on policy, you can set backpressure to queue up to some ms, or fail fast to hosted fallback; for user-facing real-time UI we recommend fast failover to a slightly cheaper model variant rather than blocking
[05:55] [06:00] Rajiv: about the SDK retry/backoff — our current approach is naive sleep loop, can you suggest a better pattern?
[06:08] Sofia: yes we suggest jittered exponential backoff with idempotency keys plus circuit breaker thresholds (e.g., after N consecutive 5xx for a route, fall back to degraded model). we'll add code sample in the repo
[06:20] Samir: will you also add a sample for validating structured output and converting to our internal canonical object? that would speed our integration
[06:27] Sofia: absolutely, i'll add a validator util that returns (ok:false, errors:[...]) and a transform function with mapping hints
[06:34] Rajiv: quick tangent — any notes on token accounting with streaming responses? we sometimes get double-charge concerns from streaming + final chunk 
[06:43] Liam: streaming counts are measured as emitted tokens; finalization shouldn't double-charge but we'll share an annotated example of how tokens are billed in a streaming + function-call workflow
[06:55] Evelyn: thanks, that doc will help finance and our cloud cost folks reconcile the numbers
[07:01] [07:30] Liam: ok lets walk through the failing payload that samir mentioned, can you screen share the raw trace?
[07:39] Samir: yep putting it in the chat now — the payload is large, note the base64 blobs and the long conversation history repeated because of a previous bug
